title: Working PRD Draft — Console Route-level A/B Testing Framework

Confluence: ADR-0188 Experiment exposure logging and privacy
content:
Doc status: WORKING DRAFT (not yet aligned). This is a PRD scratchpad intended to capture product direction + open questions for Route-level A/B testing in Console. Expect inconsistencies.

Owner: Marissa (Console & Rollouts)
PM partners: Paula (telemetry requirements)
Eng lead: Dylan (Console & Tooling)
Design lead: Tessa
SRE: Sean
Evals: Jonas

Last edit notes (2026-02-10):
- Added early partner quotes + clarified “results” scope for Beta.
- Captured tier gating debate (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and a pricing strawman.
- Added additional guardrail questions from SRE.

============================================================
1) Summary / why we’re doing this
============================================================
Customers want to compare model variants/configurations in production with: (a) deterministic traffic split, (b) measurement they can trust, and (c) safe rollback when things go sideways.

We have rollout primitives today (canaries, pinning, fallback). Customers are re-creating “experiments” by manually duplicating routes + doing client-side splits + correlating logs. This breaks down quickly:
- inconsistent assignment (esp. retries/streaming),
- difficult to isolate routing changes vs model changes,
- no standard exposure logging => results don’t line up across dashboards,
- operational risk (traffic shifting without guardrails) is scary for enterprise.

Proposed: a Console-first Route-level A/B testing framework that extends existing routing and telemetry to support experiments with deterministic assignment + standardized reporting.

============================================================
2) Target users + jobs-to-be-done
============================================================
Personas
A) ML engineer / applied ML
- Wants to run “model A vs model B” safely on prod traffic, then decide on default.
- Needs quality signal (offline eval suite) plus cost/latency comparison.

B) Platform engineer / infra owner
- Wants standardized experimentation that doesn’t blow up telemetry cardinality.
- Needs safe operational controls: audit logs, approvals (or at least RBAC), rollback.

C) Product engineer
- Wants a simple way to test different prompting / configs / model versions on a route.

Primary JTBD
- “Split traffic for /v1/chat/completions in Project X between (control) and (treatment), measure latency/cost/errors, and stop if it regresses.”

Secondary JTBD
- “Attach an eval suite so we can compare quality deltas pre/post shipping.”

Non-goals (v1)
- Multi-armed bandits / auto-optimization.
- Arbitrary custom metrics ingestion.
- Client-side SDK experimentation helpers (beyond docs).

============================================================
3) Problem statement (customer pain) + evidence
============================================================
What we hear today:
- “We can’t trust our A/B results because retries + streaming re-connects flip the variant.”
- “We need a one-click rollback. Our org won’t allow experimentation without guardrails.”
- “We can’t reconcile cost across variants because token and GPU costs show up in different dashboards.”

Early customer / prospect requests (verbatim-ish notes; anonymized; dates approximate)
1) Enterprise prospect (security-heavy):
   “If you’re going to let developers shift production traffic, we need audit logs and role-based permissions. Otherwise this won’t pass review.”

2) Mid-market SaaS (LLM features in workflow product):
   “We want 90/10 for a week, then 50/50, then decide. If p95 gets worse by ~10% we want it to auto-stop.”

3) AI-native startup:
   “We basically want ‘LaunchDarkly for models’ but with cost and latency built in.”

4) Regulated industry design partner candidate:
   “We can’t send prompts off-network. If this is hosted-only, it’s a no-go; if you can support VPC later, we’ll start on Dedicated now.”

============================================================
4) Goals + success metrics
============================================================
Product goals (Beta)
- Customers can create an experiment at the route level in Console with a clear traffic allocation (e.g., 90/10, 50/50).
- Deterministic assignment is stable (no flipping across retries/stream reconnect) given documented inputs.
- Results dashboard shows the minimum set of trustworthy metrics and clearly labels sample sizes and confidence.
- Guardrails and rollback are operationally safe (SRE sign-off).

Success metrics (measure after Beta starts)
Adoption
- # of orgs enabling A/B testing
- # experiments created + % that reach a “decision” state (stopped because winner chosen vs abandoned)
- # routes under experiment

Reliability/quality of platform
- % of experiments with assignment anomalies (variant drift vs configured split) flagged by system
- % of experiments triggering guardrails / auto-rollback (should exist but not be noisy)
- Support burden: # tickets / experiment; top categories

Reporting integrity
- Delta between Console-reported latency and canonical service latency dashboards within tolerance (define tolerance)

============================================================
5) Scope: what is included in v1 vs later
============================================================
In scope (v1)
- Console workflows: create → validate → start/stop → rollback
- Route-level policy object with deterministic bucketing
- Exposure logging (standard event) emitted at gateway, low overhead
- Aggregated reporting for:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, end-to-end
  - request counts, exposures, split drift
  - token counts, per-request cost attribution (token + GPU where available)
  - error and timeout rates (including 429s)
- Basic statistical comparison in UI for common metrics (at least: relative deltas + confidence indicator; exact stats TBD)
- Optional: attach offline eval suite (Redwood eval harness) to compute quality deltas (batch/offline; not real-time)
- Audit logs for experiment lifecycle actions

Not in scope (v1)
- Online judge sampling pipelines managed end-to-end (may be “bring your own” initially)
- Arbitrary custom metric ingestion
- Multi-armed bandit / automated traffic steering
- Full-on “approval workflows” (might be enterprise request; revisit)

Follow-ons (likely)
- Private/VPC support parity
- Exportable experiment report PDF/CSV for audit / exec review
- Programmatic API for experiment CRUD (beyond internal Console APIs)

============================================================
6) User experience (draft)
============================================================
Console entry point
- Project → Routes → “Experiments” tab (or a route detail page with “Start experiment”)

Create experiment fields (draft)
- Name + description
- Route selector (explicit: route + method + project)
- Eligibility
  - Environment: prod/staging
  - Region selection (optional)
  - Tenant selection (default: all tenants in project)
- Assignment key (IMPORTANT; see open questions)
  - Default: “api_key_id + tenant_id” (if available) (TBD)
- Variants
  - Variant A (“Control”) config (model + version + parameters)
  - Variant B (“Treatment”) config
  - (Maybe allow >2 variants later; v1 may allow 2 only)
- Split
  - 90/10, 50/50, etc.
- Schedule
  - Start now / at time
  - Stop at time (optional)
- Guardrails (defaults + editable by role?)
  - Max p95 regression threshold
  - Max error rate threshold
  - Minimum exposure count before evaluating

Validate step
- Pre-flight checks
  - overlapping experiments on same route?
  - incompatible model type differences? (e.g. embeddings vs chat)
  - required telemetry fields present?
  - cardinality check (tag allowlist)

Results dashboard (Beta)
- Overview
  - exposures by variant
  - configured vs actual split
  - decision status (running/paused/stopped/rolled back)
- Metrics
  - latency (p50/p95/p99, TTFT)
  - cost (avg cost/request, avg tokens)
  - errors (rate, 429s)
- Confidence / interpretation hints
  - show sample size per variant
  - show “not enough data” warnings

============================================================
7) Tier gating + availability (DEBATE)
============================================================
Current proposal options (needs decision)

Option 1: Beta only on Dedicated (plus internal)
Pros
- Safer: fewer customers, more predictable configs
- Better supportability; easier to do hands-on onboarding
- Aligns with enterprise ask for reliability/guardrails
Cons
- Limits PLG learning; we may miss “fast feedback” from Hosted-heavy users
- Risk: perception that Console experimentation is “enterprise-only” feature

Option 2: Beta on Hosted + Dedicated (flagged), with default guardrails strict on Hosted
Pros
- More feedback; faster iteration on UI and results
- Great marketing moment for developer-first platform
Cons
- Potential cost/risk: more experiments running means more telemetry + more confusion tickets
- Risk of misuse (traffic shifting) without enough enterprise controls

Option 3: Hosted only for results-lite; Dedicated gets full results + guardrails
Pros
- Lets Hosted users “try” the workflow
- Keeps expensive/complex reporting and guardrails limited
Cons
- Frustrating: “Why can’t I see the metrics?” Might backfire.

Private / VPC
- Not Beta (tentative). A lot of v1 assumes centralized telemetry pipelines and existing Console reporting datasets.
- We should be explicit that Private is “targeted follow-on” once event schema and aggregation are stable.

Decision needed by: Phase 0 end (so Eng can build entitlements/flags correctly)
Owner: Marissa + Priya + Sean (SRE) + Sales input

============================================================
8) Pricing & packaging (strawman, not final)
============================================================
Assumptions
- Base capability (routing split) is mostly “platform feature” but it unlocks high value.
- Reporting + retention + eval integration have real infra cost (telemetry storage + compute).

Strawman packaging ideas
A) Include basic A/B experimentation (create/run + basic dashboard) in Hosted Pro and Dedicated.
   Add-on for advanced reporting + long retention + eval integration.

B) Make A/B a Dedicated/Enterprise feature initially.
   Hosted gets “canary rollouts only” (status quo).

C) Charge per active experiment per month (metered), plus included bundle for enterprise.
   (Concern: might discourage adoption and increase support friction.)

Pricing sensitivity notes (from GTM anecdotes)
- Enterprise is willing to pay for audit/export/compliance plus “quality reporting” if it replaces internal tooling.
- Startups want it included; they compare to “free” DIY.

Open question: Is the thing we monetize the experimentation engine, or the quality/eval layer, or long-term analytics?

============================================================
9) Requirements (product + technical)
============================================================
Functional requirements
- Deterministic assignment must be stable and documented.
- Must not require customer code changes beyond optional headers (ideally none).
- Ability to start/stop experiment without redeploying anything.
- Ability to rollback to control quickly.
- Results should be available with reasonable freshness (define: within 5–10 min?)

Telemetry requirements (minimum)
- Exposure event emitted for each request that is eligible
- Must include experiment_id + variant_id, route, project, region, timestamp, and request outcome fields
- Metrics aggregated per variant with consistent definitions (TTFT, end-to-end latency, tokens)
- Must avoid high-cardinality tags (no user_id raw, no prompt content)

Security/compliance requirements
- Audit logs: create/update/start/stop/rollback; who/when/what changed
- RBAC: who can create and who can start/stop; at minimum align with existing “Rollouts admin” role
- Privacy: no PII in exposure logs; hashed IDs only; retention policy

Operational requirements (SRE)
- Guardrails with clear defaults
- Alerting + runbook; ability to emergency-disable experiments for a project
- Safe failure behavior (if assignment service fails, default to control? or fallback policy?)

============================================================
10) Risks / edge cases (known)
============================================================
- Assignment drift due to incorrect bucketing, uneven hash distribution, or missing hash key headers.
- Streaming retries reconnecting and being treated as new requests.
- Overlapping rollouts: canary + experiment both defined on same route. Need precedence.
- Metrics mismatch: customer compares our p95 to theirs, sees mismatch because of sampling windows, definitions (TTFT vs first byte), etc.
- Telemetry cardinality explosion if customers create many experiments or if we allow free-form tags.
- Customer misinterpretation of “confidence” and small sample sizes.

============================================================
11) Open questions (needs alignment)
============================================================
Product / UX
1) Two variants only in v1, or allow N variants (max 3)?
   - If N>2, reporting and UI complexity increases quickly.

2) Terminology: “Control/Treatment” vs “Variant A/B”.
   - Support thread risk: customers interpret “control” as default model.

3) Should we allow “paused” state (stop routing but keep config)?

Tier gating
4) Beta: Dedicated-only vs Hosted+Dedicated?
5) Private: explicitly out of scope for Beta, but do we promise timeline?

Pricing
6) Is this monetized at all at Beta? If yes, what is included?

Assignment inputs
7) What is the default stickiness key?
   Candidates we’ve heard:
   - tenant_id + api_key_id (stable, available)
   - x-user-id header (customer-provided; may be missing; can cause flipping)
   - request_id (bad; not stable)
   Need a “best effort” fallback chain that does not create silent variant flipping.

Stats + reporting
8) What statistics do we show in Console for Beta?
   - “Confidence” label is risky; may imply more rigor than we can guarantee.
   - Alternative: show deltas + bands + “directional only” disclaimer.

Guardrails
9) Defaults: what thresholds are safe by default?
   - Proposed starting point: auto-rollback if p95 +15% AND >N exposures AND sustained 10min
   - Error rate thresholds: more strict for 429s?

10) Who gets paged/alerted for guardrail triggers?
   - Customer-only? Redwood SRE? Both?

============================================================
12) Beta plan (rough)
============================================================
Beta candidate profile
- Teams already using rollouts/canaries
- Has clear model decision to make (not just curiosity)
- Will commit to sharing feedback and joining weekly sync

Beta size
- 2–3 design partners (Phase 2), expand to ~10 after stability

What we need from partners
- Agreement on assignment key semantics (e.g., whether they can pass user identifier header)
- Agreement on what they consider “success metrics” for the experiment

============================================================
13) Appendix — notes from conversations
============================================================
Support pain points to preempt (from past rollouts)
- Confusion when results don’t match customer dashboards
- Confusion around “variant names” and assuming variant A is always default

Design notes (Tessa)
- Make the create flow feel like “rollout” not “data science experiment”
- Warnings on overlap and “this will shift prod traffic” should be explicit

Telemetry notes (Paula/Logan)
- Keep the event schema small; ship v1 with a locked allowlist
- We need a way to sample exposures without biasing results (or show sampling clearly)

SRE notes (Sean)
- Emergency disable must exist before enabling Beta broadly
- Guardrail automation needs to be auditable and safe (no flapping)

============================================================
Next steps / asks
============================================================
- Marissa: schedule decision meeting on tier gating + Beta scope (include Priya, Dylan, Sean, Sales rep)
- Paula/Logan: propose minimal metrics schema + retention/sampling plan for Beta
- Dylan/Chloe/Jada: confirm precedence rules vs canary/fallback (tie to ADR)
- Jonas/Sana: propose “Console-safe” statistical language and minimum sample size messaging
